A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SlotAdapt and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices A.1–A.4. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite appendix table relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SlotAdapt segmentation, representation-probing, reconstruction and compositional-editing results, including quantitative comparisons and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains the original SlotAdapt experiments, numerical results and qualitative examples in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The slot encoder, frozen diffusion decoder, adapter conditioning, pooled register token and attention-guidance objectives remain unchanged. SlotAdapt's own implementation already specifies DINOv2 in v1; the revised baseline-encoder statement does not establish a proposed-method change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MOVi-E, VOC and COCO, with the same segmentation, representation-probing, reconstruction and compositional-editing coverage. SPOT is compared on existing datasets; newly explicit COCO labels in ablation captions identify retained experiments.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4 expands the GLASS comparison in v1 Table 12 to include SPOT w/o ENS and SPOT w/ ENS on both VOC and COCO in v3 Table 11. Existing comparators remain, making this a limited addition of one comparator family.

E3.justification: Section 4's Baselines paragraph changes the stated frozen encoder for all real-world models from DINO to DINOv2. This revises a reported experimental setting, although unchanged scores and v1's existing DINOv2 implementation description do not establish that experiments were rerun. Splits, budgets, preprocessing and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The conditioning-block, register-token, guidance-strategy, BOQ-SA, slot-count, guidance-timing and classifier-free-guidance ablations are retained with identical results. Qualitative examples are also unchanged. Expanded captions and relocated tables do not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added SPOT rows retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 Table 11 adds SPOT results on VOC and COCO; for example, SPOT w/ ENS has COCO FG-ARI/mBOi/mBOc scores of 37.8/35.0/44.7. All previously reported numerical entries and visual examples are retained, so no improved SlotAdapt performance is demonstrated.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and their mathematical definitions, attention formulations and loss construction are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and principal claims: adapter-based slot conditioning, guidance without external supervision, and successful compositional generation on complex real-world images, including COCO.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds an interpretation of SPOT's segmentation performance and attributes SlotAdapt's advantage in instance differentiation to its higher FG-ARI. Figures 11 and 13 replace absolute non-fragmentation wording with a tendency toward fewer fragments; Figure 15 changes 'solve' to 'mitigate' the part-whole problem. The conclusion's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 removes A.1's statements that code and training scripts accompany the supplementary material and that code will be released upon publication. The project-page link and technical specifications remain. Ablation captions now explicitly identify COCO. These are documentation changes; actual code availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds Kakogeorgiou et al. (2024), describing SPOT's self-training and patch-order permutation in Section 2.1 and contrasting its supervision, segmentation and generation coverage with SlotAdapt in A.4. The remaining references and research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Changes comprise expanded affiliations, localized prose and grammar edits, clearer appendix captions, and an A.4 heading and discussion expanded to include SPOT. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V3 moves Table 6 from page 18 to page 17, removes v1's duplicate slot-count caption, and renumbers subsequent tables. It expands ablation captions and the comparison table with SPOT rows, and slightly resizes Figure 15 to improve page fit. Figure content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The SPOT comparison supplies useful context against another fully unsupervised method, while clearer ablation captions, corrected table presentation and more cautious segmentation wording improve interpretability. These are limited gains to an unchanged method and experimental foundation. Removing explicit supplementary-code and release statements weakens reproducibility guidance, although the project link and technical details remain; actual resource availability is unresolved.
